Exit code 1
# Classification guide excerpt

Linden Shore Mutual, workers' compensation, Maryland. Edition of July 2025. Internal use by underwriting and premium
audit.

This excerpt holds the general paragraphs and the class codes our current new-business employers fall under. Audit
files cite a paragraph by its identifier (CG-01, CG-02 and so on). A class code is cited by the paragraph that
describes it.

## General

**CG-01. Premium basis.** Premium is charged per USD 100 of payroll in each class code at the rate underwriting sets
for that code. Payroll is reported for the policy period being audited.

**CG-02. Assigning codes.** An employer is assigned the class code that describes its principal business. An employee
whose work is described by another code in this guide is reported under that code. An employer may carry several codes.

**CG-03. Payroll.** Payroll is the gross remuneration paid to employees for the period: wages, salaries, commissions
and bonuses. Expense reimbursements that the employer can document, such as travel and lodging costs, are not payroll.

**CG-05. Owners and executive officers.** An owner or executive officer who has filed an election of exclusion is not
counted. An owner who is included is counted under the code for the work the owner does.

**CG-06. Subcontractors.** Payments to a subcontractor who does not carry workers' compensation insurance for its own
workers may be treated as payroll of the employer, under the code for the work the subcontractor performed.

**CG-07. Division of payroll.** When an employee performs work in more than one classification and the employer keeps
records of the time spent in each, the employee's payroll may be divided between the codes.

## Class codes

**CG-04. C-110 Clerical office employees.** Employees whose duties are confined to an office: correspondence,
bookkeeping, dispatching by telephone or radio, drafting and estimating at a desk, and professional staff who work in
the office.

**CG-11. R-310 Roofing.** Installation, repair and removal of roofs and roof coverings on any building, including
work on scaffolds and ladders at the roof line.

**CG-12. R-320 Siding and gutters.** Installation and repair of exterior siding, gutters, downspouts and exterior trim
below the roof line. Roofing work is described by CG-11.

**CG-13. L-620 Landscaping and lawn care.** Lawn mowing, planting, mulching and the care of grounds.

**CG-15. H-420 Residential homebuilding.** Construction and remodeling of dwellings: framing, drywall, interior
finish, carpentry and general labor at the building site. Roofing work is described by CG-11 and electrical wiring
by CG-21.

**CG-21. E-510 Electrical wiring.** Installation and repair of electrical wiring and fixtures inside buildings,
including service connections.

**CG-22. M-830 Metal fabrication shop.** Cutting, bending and welding of sheet and structural metal in a shop.

**CG-31. T-610 Courier and delivery drivers.** Drivers of vans and light trucks delivering parcels and documents,
and helpers who ride on the delivery vehicles.

**CG-35. G-950 Parking garage attendants.** Parking and retrieving customer vehicles.

**CG-41. F-710 Restaurants.** Preparation and service of meals: kitchen staff, servers, hosts and dishwashers.

**CG-42. F-720 Off-site caterers.** Preparation of food and its service at events away from the employer's premises,
including the catering crew of an employer that also runs a restaurant.

**CG-51. N-910 Home health care.** Personal care and nursing services in clients' homes.

# Linden Shore Mutual premium audit house practice

The written rules are the classification guide excerpt (paragraphs `CG-nn`). The guide is the authoritative version of
the rules (interview 1, 08:41 PM). This file records the audit team's unwritten house practice exactly as Nadia Brennan,
Senior Premium Auditor, stated it in interview 1 (`interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261027-0049.md`).

The `HP-n` labels are this Skill's own labels for traceability. They are **not** company identifiers. Never put them in
the `rationale_ref` column, which takes only the guide's own `CG-nn` identifiers.

Where house practice and the guide differ, house practice is how this team applies the guide, and the report says so.
When a case is not covered here, there is no rule. Do not write one up as if it were the team's. Propose a treatment,
say why, and mark it as an open item for the auditor (08:43 PM).

| Label | Practice | Source (interview 1) |
|---|---|---|
| HP-1 | Classify people by what they actually do, not by job title. Employers lean their own split toward the clerical code. | 08:43 PM |
| HP-2 | Do not split one person's pay between codes. The only exception is dispatchers or inside employees who ride on delivery routes. Their pay is split by whole weeks, based on the route log. Sign-in logs or timesheets track the days spent on specific duties. | 08:44 PM |
| HP-3 | An owner who performs any field work is counted at a flat USD 63,700. | 08:44 PM |
| HP-4 | Clerical staff are C-110 unless they are on a job site five or more days. | 08:44 PM |
| HP-5 | Payments to uninsured subcontractors are added to payroll at 60% of the amount paid, under the applicable code. | 08:44 PM |
| HP-6 | For crews working out of town, a daily allowance up to USD 47 per worker per day is left out of payroll. Anything paid above that counts as payroll under that worker's code. | 08:44 PM |
| HP-7 | The records in the file decide the allocation. Any difference from what the employer reported goes on that employer's question list so the employer can confirm the record. | 08:45 PM |
| HP-8 | For each discrepancy, record the specific payment or value found in the records and the exact document or log that is the evidence. | 08:46 PM |
| HP-9 | Every adjustment, and the record each decision rests on, must be on the question list. A question is actionable if it names the person, days or payment, and the document needed to confirm. | 08:47 PM |
| HP-10 | A case house practice does not cover: propose a treatment, write down why, and mark it as an open item for the auditor to confirm. | 08:43 PM, 08:46 PM, 08:47 PM |
| HP-11 | Process each employer individually. The auditor reviews the results and the proposed gray-area handling before they count as audit work. | 08:48 PM, 08:49 PM |
| HP-12 | The auditor needs to know which two employers to call first before Friday's quotes, and why. | 08:47 PM, 08:48 PM |

## Stated gaps (no rule exists, so every such case is an open item)

- Supervisors and temporary workers: "I have no specific rules" (08:44 PM).
- Overtime, bonuses, tips and other payroll components beyond the out-of-town allowance: nothing was stated. CG-03
  (gross remuneration, including bonuses) applies.

## How this Skill reads the practice (assumptions, each flagged in every report where it matters)

These readings are the Skill's interpretation, not the auditor's words. Each one is surfaced as an open item wherever it
changes an allocation.

- **A1 (HP-2 "by whole weeks").** A pay week in which the inside employee appears as a ride-along on at least one route
  day goes entirely to the route code. Every other week stays under the employee's own code.
- **A2 (HP-2, no split elsewhere).** When crew timesheets record more than one type of work for one person, the whole
  of that person's pay goes to the code with the most recorded hours. A tie is an open item. CG-07 would permit a
  division. House practice says not to, and the report shows the margin.
- **A3 (HP-4 "five or more days").** Counted as distinct dates in the audit period on which the employee signed in at a
  job site (site sign-in log) or worked a crew timesheet. The code that replaces C-110 is the code of the work done at
  the sites visited most. The guide and house practice do not say which code it is, so this is always an open item.
- **A4 (HP-3).** The flat amount applies to an owner who is included under CG-05, meaning no election of exclusion is on
  file. It is counted under the code for the field work the owner does (CG-05), whatever the register shows as paid.
- **A5 (HP-5).** A subcontractor is treated as insured for a payment only when a certificate in the file covers the
  payment date. When a certificate's name differs from the payee name, the match is an open item.
- **A6 (HP-6).** The cap is USD 47 times the travel days recorded for that worker. An allowance paid with no recorded
  travel days is payroll in full.

"""Apply the classification guide and the audit team's house practice to one employer's records.

The worksheet (written per employer by the analyst running the Skill) supplies the judgments the records cannot make on
their own: the code that describes each person's actual duties, which code each type of crew work, job site and
subcontracted trade falls under, and owner status. Everything that is arithmetic or a stated house rule is applied here,
from the records, the same way for every employer.
"""

import datetime
import itertools
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

from .records import CENT, day, money

FIXED_HOLIDAYS = {(1, 1): "New Year's Day", (7, 4): "Independence Day", (12, 25): "Christmas Day"}


class WorksheetError(ValueError):
    pass


@dataclass
class Line:
    code: str
    amount: Decimal
    basis: str


@dataclass
class Person:
    id: str
    name: str
    position: str
    wages: Decimal
    lines: list = field(default_factory=list)
    records: list = field(default_factory=list)
    employer_code: str | None = None

    @property
    def primary_code(self):
        return max(self.lines, key=lambda l: l.amount).code


@dataclass
class Adjustment:
    about: str
    kind: str
    amount: Decimal
    code: str
    detail: str
    records: list
    rule: str


@dataclass
class OpenItem:
    about: str
    proposal: str
    why: str
    records: list
    rule: str = "HP-10"


@dataclass
class Result:
    rec: dict
    ws: dict
    people: list = field(default_factory=list)
    sub_lines: list = field(default_factory=list)
    adjustments: list = field(default_factory=list)
    open_items: list = field(default_factory=list)
    questions: list = field(default_factory=list)
    notes: list = field(default_factory=list)
    totals: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    inference: str = ""

    @property
    def employer_split(self):
        return {c: v["payroll"] for c, v in self.rec["employer_split"].items()}

    def differences(self):
        codes = sorted(set(self.totals) | set(self.employer_split))
        return {c: self.totals.get(c, Decimal("0.00")) - self.employer_split.get(c, Decimal("0.00")) for c in codes}

    @property
    def accepts_employer_split(self):
        return all(d == 0 for d in self.differences().values()) and not any(
            p.employer_code and {l.code for l in p.lines} != {p.employer_code} for p in self.people)


def _uniq(items):
    return list(dict.fromkeys(i for i in items if i))


def fmt(amount):
    return f"{amount:,.2f}"


def infer_employer_codes(register, split):
    """Find the one assignment of register employees to the employer's codes that reproduces its split.

    Returns (mapping or None, explanation). The application gives only a head count and payroll per code, so a
    per-person reading of the employer's split is an inference and is labelled as one.
    """
    codes = list(split)
    if len(codes) ** len(register) > 3_000_000:
        return None, "too many employees to infer the employer's per-person split from its totals"
    hits = []
    for combo in itertools.product(codes, repeat=len(register)):
        counts, sums = Counter(combo), defaultdict(Decimal)
        if any(counts[c] != split[c]["employees"] for c in codes):
            continue
        for code, e in zip(combo, register):
            sums[code] += e["wages"]
        if all(sums[c] == split[c]["payroll"] for c in codes):
            hits.append(dict(zip((e["id"] for e in register), combo)))
            if len(hits) > 1:
                return None, "more than one way to read the employer's split per person; it is compared by code only"
    if not hits:
        return None, ("no assignment of register wages reproduces the employer's split exactly; "
                      "it is compared by code only")
    return hits[0], ("the employer's per-person codes are inferred: exactly one assignment of the register's wages "
                     "reproduces its reported head count and payroll for every code")


def allocate(guide, hp, rec, ws):
    res = Result(rec, ws)
    clerical = hp["clerical_code"]
    threshold = int(hp["clerical_job_site_day_threshold"])
    owner_flat = money(hp["owner_field_work_flat_payroll"])
    sub_share = Decimal(hp["uninsured_subcontractor_payroll_share"])
    allowance_cap = money(hp["out_of_town_daily_allowance_exclusion"])
    start, end = rec["period"]
    in_period = lambda d: start <= d <= end  # noqa: E731
    reg_file = rec["register_file"]

    def code_ok(code, where):
        try:
            guide.ref_for(code)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise WorksheetError(f"{where}: {exc}") from None
        return code

    ws_people = ws.get("employees", {})
    missing = [e["id"] for e in rec["register"] if e["id"] not in ws_people]
    extra = [i for i in ws_people if i not in {e["id"] for e in rec["register"]}]
    if missing or extra:
        raise WorksheetError(f"worksheet employees do not match {reg_file}: missing {missing or 'none'}, "
                             f"not on register {extra or 'none'}")

    def out_of_period(rows, key, file):
        n = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get(key) and not in_period(day(r[key])))
        if n:
            res.notes.append(f"{n} row(s) in {file} fall outside the audit period and were not used.")

    # Index the supporting records, audit period only.
    timesheets = defaultdict(list)
    for r in rec["timesheets"]:
        if in_period(day(r["date"])):
            timesheets[r["employee_id"]].append(r)
    out_of_period(rec["timesheets"], "date", rec["timesheets_file"])

    site_days = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(set))
    for r in rec["signins"]:
        if r["employee_id"] and in_period(day(r["date"])):
            site_days[r["employee_id"]][day(r["date"])].add(r["site"])
    others = [r for r in rec["signins"] if not r["employee_id"]]
    if others:
        res.notes.append(f"{len(others)} sign-in row(s) in {rec['signins_file']} have no employee ID "
                         f"({', '.join(sorted({r.get('name', '?') for r in others}))}); they are not employees and were not used.")
    out_of_period(rec["signins"], "date", rec["signins_file"])

    ride_days = defaultdict(set)
    for r in rec["route_log"]:
        if r["ride_along_id"] and in_period(day(r["date"])):
            ride_days[r["ride_along_id"]].add(day(r["date"]))
    out_of_period(rec["route_log"], "date", rec["route_log_file"])

    weekly = defaultdict(list)
    for r in rec["weekly_payroll"]:
        weekly[r["employee_id"]].append((day(r["week_start"]), day(r["week_end"]), money(r["gross_pay"])))

    work_codes = ws.get("work_type_codes", {})
    site_codes = ws.get("site_codes", {})
    route_code = ws.get("route_code") and code_ok(ws["route_code"], "route_code")
    split_people, ride_people = [], []

    for e in rec["register"]:
        w = ws_people[e["id"]]
        duty = code_ok(w.get("duty_code") or "", f"employees.{e['id']}.duty_code")
        p = Person(e["id"], e["name"], e["position"], e["wages"], records=[reg_file] + w.get("records", []))
        owner = ws.get("owners", {}).get(e["id"])

        if owner and owner.get("included") and owner.get("field_work"):
            code = code_ok(owner.get("field_code") or duty, f"owners.{e['id']}.field_code")
            p.records += owner.get("records", [])
            p.lines = [Line(code, owner_flat, f"Included owner who does field work ({owner['basis']}). Counted at the "
                                              f"flat {fmt(owner_flat)} (HP-3) under the code for the work done (CG-05).")]
            res.adjustments.append(Adjustment(
                e["name"], "Owner counted at flat amount", owner_flat, code,
                f"{reg_file} shows wages of {fmt(e['wages'])}. House practice counts an owner who does any field work at "
                f"{fmt(owner_flat)}, under {code}, the code for the work done.", _uniq(p.records), "HP-3, CG-05"))
            res.people.append(p)
            continue

        final, basis = duty, w["basis"]
        hours = timesheets.get(e["id"])
        if hours:
            by_code, by_type = defaultdict(Decimal), defaultdict(Decimal)
            for r in hours:
                if r["work_type"] not in work_codes:
                    raise WorksheetError(f"work type {r['work_type']!r} in {rec['timesheets_file']} has no entry in "
                                         f"worksheet work_type_codes")
                code = code_ok(work_codes[r["work_type"]], f"work_type_codes.{r['work_type']}")
                by_code[code] += Decimal(r["hours"])
                by_type[r["work_type"]] += Decimal(r["hours"])
            ranked = sorted(by_code.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])
            leaders = [c for c, h in ranked if h == ranked[0][1]]
            final = duty if duty in leaders else leaders[0]
            mix = ", ".join(f"{t} {h:g} h" for t, h in sorted(by_type.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]))
            basis = (f"Crew timesheets: {mix}. The whole of the pay goes to {final}, the code with the most recorded "
                     f"hours (HP-2: one person's pay is not split; reading A2).")
            p.records.append(rec["timesheets_file"])
            if len(by_code) > 1:
                split_people.append((p, dict(by_code), final))
            if len(leaders) > 1:
                res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                    e["name"], f"Report all of {e['name']}'s pay under {final}.",
                    f"The timesheets show equal hours under {', '.join(leaders)}, and house practice does not say how "
                    f"to break a tie.", [rec["timesheets_file"]]))
        elif duty == clerical and site_days.get(e["id"]):
            days = site_days[e["id"]]
            p.records.append(rec["signins_file"])
            dates = ", ".join(d.isoformat() for d in sorted(days))
            for d in sorted(days):
                if (d.month, d.day) in FIXED_HOLIDAYS:
                    res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                        f"{e['name']}: sign-in on {d.isoformat()}",
                        "Count the day as recorded, because the records decide (HP-7).",
                        f"{rec['signins_file']} records {e['name']} at {', '.join(sorted(days[d]))} on "
                        f"{FIXED_HOLIDAYS[(d.month, d.day)]}. This may be a recording error.", [rec["signins_file"]]))
            if len(days) < threshold:
                basis += (f" {rec['signins_file']} shows {len(days)} job-site day(s) ({dates}), fewer than "
                          f"{threshold}, so the person stays {clerical} (HP-4).")
            else:
                unmapped = sorted({s for sites in days.values() for s in sites if s not in site_codes})
                if unmapped:
                    raise WorksheetError(f"site(s) {unmapped} in {rec['signins_file']} have no entry in worksheet "
                                         f"site_codes (use null when no code in the guide describes the work there)")
                code_days = Counter()
                for sites in days.values():
                    for c in {site_codes[s] for s in sites} - {None}:
                        code_days[c] += 1
                chosen = w.get("field_code")
                ranked = code_days.most_common()
                if not chosen and ranked:
                    leaders = [c for c, n in ranked if n == ranked[0][1]]
                    chosen = leaders[0] if len(leaders) == 1 else None
                    if len(leaders) > 1:
                        res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                            e["name"], f"Keep {e['name']} under {clerical} until the employer confirms the work at the sites.",
                            f"The sites visited split evenly between {', '.join(leaders)}.", [rec["signins_file"]]))
                site_mix = ", ".join(f"{c} {n} day(s)" for c, n in ranked) or "no code in the guide describes the site work"
                if chosen:
                    final = code_ok(chosen, f"employees.{e['id']}.field_code")
                    basis = (f"{w['basis']} {rec['signins_file']} shows {len(days)} job-site days ({dates}), so the "
                             f"person is not clerical (HP-4: {threshold} or more days). Days by site code: {site_mix}. "
                             f"The person is reported under {final} (reading A3).")
                    res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                        e["name"], f"Report all {fmt(e['wages'])} of {e['name']}'s pay under {final} instead of {clerical}.",
                        f"{len(days)} job-site days is at or above the {threshold}-day threshold (HP-4). House practice "
                        f"does not say which code replaces {clerical}. {final} is the code of the work at the sites "
                        f"visited ({site_mix}).", [rec["signins_file"]] + w.get("records", [])))
                else:
                    basis += (f" {rec['signins_file']} shows {len(days)} job-site days ({dates}), but no code in the "
                              f"guide describes the work at those sites, so the person stays {clerical}.")
                    res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                        e["name"], f"Keep {e['name']} under {clerical}.",
                        f"{len(days)} job-site days meets the {threshold}-day threshold (HP-4), but no code in the guide "
                        f"describes the work at the sites ({', '.join(sorted({s for v in days.values() for s in v}))}). "
                        f"House practice does not say what happens then.", [rec["signins_file"]] + w.get("records", [])))
        p.lines = [Line(final, e["wages"], basis)]

        rides = ride_days.get(e["id"])
        if route_code and rides and final != route_code:
            weeks = sorted(weekly.get(e["id"], []))
            p.records += [rec["route_log_file"]]
            if not weeks:
                res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                    e["name"], f"Leave all of {e['name']}'s pay under {final}.",
                    f"The route log shows {len(rides)} ride-along days, but there is no weekly pay record, so the "
                    f"pay cannot be split by whole weeks (HP-2).", [rec["route_log_file"]]))
            else:
                p.records.append(rec["weekly_payroll_file"])
                ride_weeks = [(s, t, g) for s, t, g in weeks if any(s <= d <= t for d in rides)]
                moved = sum((g for _, _, g in ride_weeks), Decimal("0.00"))
                weekly_total = sum((g for _, _, g in weeks), Decimal("0.00"))
                if weekly_total != e["wages"]:
                    res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                        e["name"], f"Use {reg_file} for the total and {rec['weekly_payroll_file']} for the week split.",
                        f"The weekly pay totals {fmt(weekly_total)} but {reg_file} shows {fmt(e['wages'])}.",
                        [reg_file, rec["weekly_payroll_file"]]))
                p.lines = [
                    Line(route_code, moved, f"{rec['route_log_file']} shows {len(rides)} ride-along days in "
                                            f"{len(ride_weeks)} pay weeks. Those whole weeks' pay goes to {route_code} "
                                            f"(HP-2, reading A1)."),
                    Line(final, e["wages"] - moved, f"{basis} The other {len(weeks) - len(ride_weeks)} pay weeks stay "
                                                    f"under {final}."),
                ]
                ride_people.append((p, rides, ride_weeks, weeks, moved))
                res.adjustments.append(Adjustment(
                    e["name"], "Whole-week route split", moved, route_code,
                    f"{len(rides)} ride-along days ({min(rides).isoformat()} to {max(rides).isoformat()}) fall in "
                    f"{len(ride_weeks)} of {len(weeks)} pay weeks. Those weeks' gross pay of {fmt(moved)} moves from "
                    f"{final} to {route_code}.", [rec["route_log_file"], rec["weekly_payroll_file"]], "HP-2"))

        if e["travel_allowance"]:
            tdays = e["travel_days"] or 0
            excluded = min(e["travel_allowance"], allowance_cap * tdays)
            excess = e["travel_allowance"] - excluded
            p.records.append(f"{reg_file} (travel_days, travel_allowance_paid)")
            if excess:
                p.lines.append(Line(final, excess, f"Out-of-town allowance above {fmt(allowance_cap)} per day: "
                                                   f"{fmt(e['travel_allowance'])} paid for {tdays} travel days, "
                                                   f"{fmt(excluded)} excluded (HP-6)."))
                res.adjustments.append(Adjustment(
                    e["name"], "Travel allowance above the daily exclusion", excess, final,
                    f"{fmt(e['travel_allowance'])} paid for {tdays} recorded travel days. Up to {fmt(allowance_cap)} "
                    f"per day ({fmt(excluded)}) is left out; the remaining {fmt(excess)} is payroll.",
                    [f"{reg_file} (travel_days, travel_allowance_paid)"], "HP-6"))
            if tdays == 0:
                res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                    e["name"], f"Count all {fmt(e['travel_allowance'])} of the allowance as payroll under {final}.",
                    f"{reg_file} records a travel allowance but no travel days. House practice excludes up to "
                    f"{fmt(allowance_cap)} per travel day, so with no recorded days nothing is excluded (reading A6).",
                    [reg_file]))
        p.records = _uniq(p.records)
        res.people.append(p)

    _subcontractors(res, rec, ws, code_ok, sub_share, in_period)

    if split_people:
        rows = "; ".join(f"{p.name}: " + ", ".join(f"{c} {h:g} h" for c, h in sorted(bc.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]))
                         + f" -> {f}" for p, bc, f in split_people)
        res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
            "Crew members with more than one type of work",
            "Report each person's whole pay under the code with the most recorded hours.",
            f"CG-07 allows a division when time records are kept, but house practice is that one person's pay is not "
            f"split, except for route ride-alongs (HP-2). House practice does not say which single code to use. "
            f"Hours by code: {rows}.", [rec["timesheets_file"]]))
    if ride_people:
        res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
            "Reading of 'split the pay by whole weeks'",
            "Any pay week with at least one ride-along day goes wholly to the route code (reading A1).",
            "A narrower reading, counting only weeks spent wholly on the road, would move less payroll. "
            + "; ".join(f"{p.name}: {len(r)} ride days in {len(rw)} of {len(wk)} weeks, {fmt(m)} moved"
                        for p, r, rw, wk, m in ride_people) + ".",
            [rec["route_log_file"], rec["weekly_payroll_file"]]))

    for item in ws.get("open_items", []):
        res.open_items.append(OpenItem(item["about"], item["proposal"], item["why"], item.get("records", []),
                                       item.get("rule", "HP-10")))

    totals = defaultdict(Decimal)
    for line in [l for p in res.people for l in p.lines] + res.sub_lines:
        totals[line.code] += line.amount
    res.totals = {c: v.quantize(CENT) for c, v in sorted(totals.items()) if v}

    mapping, res.inference = infer_employer_codes(rec["register"], rec["employer_split"])
    for p in res.people:
        p.employer_code = (mapping or {}).get(p.id)
        if p.employer_code and p.primary_code != p.employer_code and not any(a.about == p.name for a in res.adjustments):
            res.adjustments.append(Adjustment(
                p.name, "Reclassified", p.wages, p.primary_code,
                f"The employer reported {p.name} ({p.position}) under {p.employer_code}. The records put the "
                f"{fmt(p.wages)} under {p.primary_code}: {p.lines[0].basis}", p.records, "HP-1, HP-7"))
        for a in res.adjustments:
            if a.about == p.name and p.employer_code and p.employer_code != a.code:
                a.detail += f" The employer reported {p.name} under {p.employer_code}."

    _questions(res, rec, ws)
    return res


def _subcontractors(res, rec, ws, code_ok, share, in_period):
    if not rec["sub_payments"]:
        return
    certs = defaultdict(list)
    for c in rec["certificates"]:
        certs[c["subcontractor"]].append((c["certificate_no"], day(c["coverage_from"]), day(c["coverage_to"])))
    matches = ws.get("subcontractor_certificate_matches", {})
    work_codes = ws.get("subcontract_work_codes", {})
    files = _uniq([rec["sub_payments_file"], rec["certificates_file"]])
    by_sub = defaultdict(list)
    for pay in rec["sub_payments"]:
        if in_period(day(pay["date"])):
            by_sub[pay["subcontractor"]].append(pay)

    for sub, pays in by_sub.items():
        cert_name = sub if sub in certs else matches.get(sub)
        if cert_name and cert_name != sub:
            res.open_items.append(OpenItem(
                sub, f"Treat the certificate issued to '{cert_name}' as {sub}'s.",
                f"{rec['sub_payments_file']} pays '{sub}', but the certificate in {rec['certificates_file']} is issued "
                f"to '{cert_name}'. The names are close but not the same.", files))
        insured, uninsured = [], []
        for pay in pays:
            d = day(pay["date"])
            cover = [c for c in certs.get(cert_name, []) if c[1] <= d <= c[2]]
            (insured if cover else uninsured).append((pay, cover))
        for pay, _ in uninsured:
            work = pay["work"]
            if work not in work_codes:
                raise WorksheetError(f"subcontracted work {work!r} has no entry in worksheet subcontract_work_codes")
            code = code_ok(work_codes[work], f"subcontract_work_codes.{work}")
            paid = money(pay["amount_paid"])
            added = (paid * share).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
            held = certs.get(cert_name, [])
            why = ("no certificate of insurance for this subcontractor is in the file" if not held else
                   "the certificate in the file (" + "; ".join(f"{n}, {f.isoformat()} to {t.isoformat()}" for n, f, t in held)
                   + f") does not cover the payment date {pay['date']}")
            res.sub_lines.append(Line(code, added, f"{share:.0%} of {fmt(paid)} paid to uninsured subcontractor {sub} "
                                                   f"(invoice {pay.get('invoice', '?')}, {pay['date']}, {work}) (HP-5, CG-06)."))
            res.adjustments.append(Adjustment(
                f"{sub}, invoice {pay.get('invoice', '?')}", "Uninsured subcontractor payment added", added, code,
                f"{fmt(paid)} paid on {pay['date']} for {work}. Because {why}, {share:.0%} ({fmt(added)}) is added to "
                f"payroll under {code}, the code for the work.", files, "HP-5, CG-06"))
        res.notes.append(f"{sub}: {len(insured)} payment(s) covered by a certificate in the file, "
                         f"{len(uninsured)} not covered.")
        res.questions.append((sub, _sub_question(sub, cert_name, insured, uninsured, rec)))


def _sub_question(sub, cert_name, insured, uninsured, rec):
    parts = []
    if insured:
        nos = sorted({c[0] for _, cov in insured for c in cov})
        parts.append(f"confirm that certificate {', '.join(nos)} covered {sub}'s own workers on the dates of invoices "
                     + ", ".join(f"{p.get('invoice', '?')} ({p['date']}, {fmt(money(p['amount_paid']))})" for p, _ in insured))
    if uninsured:
        parts.append("send a workers' compensation certificate covering the dates of invoices "
                     + ", ".join(f"{p.get('invoice', '?')} ({p['date']}, {fmt(money(p['amount_paid']))})" for p, _ in uninsured)
                     + "; without one, 60% of each payment stays in payroll")
    lead = f"{sub} ({rec['sub_payments_file']}" + (f", {rec['certificates_file']}" if rec["certificates_file"] else "") + ")"
    return f"{lead}: please " + ", and ".join(parts) + "."


def _questions(res, rec, ws):
    """Every adjustment, and every record a decision rests on, gets at least one employer question (HP-9)."""
    reg = rec["register_file"]
    adjusted = {a.about for a in res.adjustments}
    sub_qs = list(res.questions)
    res.questions = []
    q = lambda about, text: res.questions.append((about, text))  # noqa: E731

    for a in res.adjustments:
        if a.kind == "Uninsured subcontractor payment added":
            continue
        p = next((p for p in res.people if p.name == a.about), None)
        if a.kind == "Owner counted at flat amount":
            q(a.about, f"{a.about} ({reg}, site sign-in log): please confirm that {a.about} is an included owner "
                       f"(no election of exclusion on file) who did field work during the audit period, and the "
                       f"{fmt(p.wages)} of wages shown in {reg}.")
        elif a.kind == "Whole-week route split":
            q(a.about, f"{a.about} ({rec['route_log_file']}, {rec['weekly_payroll_file']}): please confirm that "
                       f"{a.about} rode along on the route days the route log records, and the weekly gross pay "
                       f"in those weeks (total {fmt(a.amount)}).")
        elif a.kind == "Travel allowance above the daily exclusion":
            row = next(e for e in rec["register"] if e["name"] == a.about)
            q(a.about, f"{a.about} ({reg}, travel columns): please confirm the {row['travel_days']} out-of-town travel "
                       f"days and the {fmt(row['travel_allowance'])} allowance paid, with the trip dates and job.")
        elif a.kind == "Reclassified":
            recs = ", ".join(r for r in p.records if r != reg)
            q(a.about, f"{a.about} ({recs or reg}): please confirm {a.about}'s actual duties during the audit period, "
                       f"and the records this first pass relied on for them: {p.lines[0].basis}")

    for p in res.people:
        if p.name in adjusted:
            continue
        if rec["timesheets_file"] in p.records:
            q(p.name, f"{p.name} ({rec['timesheets_file']}): please confirm that the crew timesheets are complete for "
                      f"{p.name} for the audit period. {p.lines[0].basis.split('. The whole')[0]}.")
        if rec["signins_file"] in p.records:
            q(p.name, f"{p.name} ({rec['signins_file']}): please confirm that the job-site sign-ins recorded for "
                      f"{p.name} are complete and correct: {p.lines[0].basis.split(rec['signins_file'])[-1].strip()}")
        travel = next((e for e in rec["register"] if e["id"] == p.id and e["travel_allowance"]), None)
        if travel:
            q(p.name, f"{p.name} ({reg}, travel columns): please confirm the {travel['travel_days']} travel days and the "
                      f"{fmt(travel['travel_allowance'])} allowance paid.")

    plain = [p for p in res.people if p.name not in adjusted]
    if plain:
        listing = "; ".join(f"{p.name}, {p.position}, {fmt(p.wages)} under {p.primary_code}" for p in plain)
        q("Payroll register", f"{reg}: please confirm that these wages are complete for the audit period "
                              f"{rec['period'][0].isoformat()} to {rec['period'][1].isoformat()}, and that each "
                              f"person's work matches the code given: {listing}.")

    res.questions += sub_qs
    for c in ws.get("confirmations", []):
        q(c["about"], c["question"])
    for item in ws.get("open_items", []):
        if item.get("employer_question"):
            q(item["about"], item["employer_question"])

"""Run the class-code-assistant first pass on one employer, several, or all of them.

Examples (from the repository root):

    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --all
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --employer patuxent-electric
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --local path/to/sources --employer new-employer
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --init-worksheet new-employer
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from cca import records, render  # noqa: E402
from cca.guide import Guide  # noqa: E402
from cca.rules import WorksheetError, allocate  # noqa: E402
from fetch_sources import fetch  # noqa: E402

SKILL_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
REFS = SKILL_DIR / "references"


def load_sources(args):
    sources = json.loads((REFS / "sources.json").read_text())
    root = Path(args.local) if args.local else Path(args.cache)
    if not args.local:
        fetch(root, sources, None if args.all else args.employer)
    manifest_path = root / "manifest.json"
    manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text()) if manifest_path.exists() else {"fetched_at": "local copy", "files": {}}
    guide_path = root / "classification-guide.md"
    if not guide_path.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"error: no classification guide at {guide_path}; the authoritative rules are required")
    guide_bytes = guide_path.read_bytes()
    run = {
        "fetched_at": manifest["fetched_at"],
        "guide_sha256": hashlib.sha256(guide_bytes).hexdigest(),
        "guide_source": sources["classification_guide"] if not args.local else str(guide_path),
        "employer_source": sources["employer_files"] if not args.local else str(root / "employers"),
    }
    return root, Guide(guide_bytes.decode("utf-8")), run


def init_worksheet(rec, path):
    """Scaffold a worksheet listing every judgment the analyst must make for this employer, with nothing filled in."""
    ws = {
        "employer": rec["employer_name"],
        "employees": {e["id"]: {"name": e["name"], "position": e["position"], "duty_code": None,
                                "basis": "TODO: the employee's actual duties and the record that shows them",
                                "records": []} for e in rec["register"]},
        "owners": {},
        "work_type_codes": {t: None for t in sorted({r["work_type"] for r in rec["timesheets"]})},
        "site_codes": {s: None for s in sorted({r["site"] for r in rec["signins"] if r["employee_id"]})},
        "route_code": None if rec["route_log"] else "n/a",
        "subcontract_work_codes": {w: None for w in sorted({r["work"] for r in rec["sub_payments"]})},
        "subcontractor_certificate_matches": {},
        "facts": [],
        "confirmations": [],
        "open_items": [],
        "unused_records": {},
    }
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if path.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"error: {path} already exists; not overwriting it")
    path.write_text(json.dumps(ws, indent=2) + "\n")


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Class code and payroll allocation first pass (Linden Shore Mutual).")
    who = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    who.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", help="every employer folder at the source location")
    who.add_argument("--employer", action="append", help="employer folder slug (repeatable)")
    who.add_argument("--init-worksheet", metavar="SLUG", help="scaffold deliverables/worksheets/SLUG.json and stop")
    ap.add_argument("--local", help="read a local copy (classification-guide.md + employers/<slug>/) instead of fetching")
    ap.add_argument("--cache", default=".cache/sources", help="where fetched sources are written (default .cache/sources)")
    ap.add_argument("--worksheets", default="deliverables/worksheets", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="deliverables", type=Path)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if args.init_worksheet:
        args.employer = [args.init_worksheet]

    root, guide, run = load_sources(args)
    slugs = sorted(p.name for p in (root / "employers").iterdir() if p.is_dir()) if args.all else args.employer
    hp = json.loads((REFS / "house_practice.json").read_text())

    if args.init_worksheet:
        path = args.worksheets / f"{args.init_worksheet}.json"
        init_worksheet(records.load(root / "employers" / args.init_worksheet), path)
        print(f"wrote {path}: fill in every null and TODO from the employer's records, then run --employer {args.init_worksheet}")
        return 0

    results = []
    for slug in slugs:
        ws_path = args.worksheets / f"{slug}.json"
        if not ws_path.exists():
            raise SystemExit(f"error: no worksheet for {slug} at {ws_path}. Run --init-worksheet {slug}, then fill it "
                             f"in from the records (see SKILL.md, step 3).")
        try:
            result = allocate(guide, hp, records.load(root / "employers" / slug), json.loads(ws_path.read_text()))
        except (records.RecordError, WorksheetError) as exc:
            raise SystemExit(f"error: {slug}: {exc}")
        render.write_codes_csv(args.out / "codes" / f"{slug}.csv", result, guide)
        results.append(result)
        print(f"{slug}: " + ", ".join(f"{c} {v:.2f}" for c, v in result.totals.items())
              + f" | adjustments {len(result.adjustments)}, open items {len(result.open_items)}, "
                f"questions {len(result.questions)}, employer split {'accepted' if result.accepts_employer_split else 'not accepted'}")

    if args.all:
        report_path, questions_path = args.out / "audit-report.md", args.out / "audit-questions.md"
    else:
        report_path = args.out / "runs" / f"{'+'.join(slugs)}-audit-report.md"
        questions_path = args.out / "runs" / f"{'+'.join(slugs)}-audit-questions.md"
    report_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    report_path.write_text(render.report(results, guide, run))
    questions_path.write_text(render.questions(results))
    (args.out / "run-manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        **run, "employers": {r.rec["file"].slug: {k: f"{v:.2f}" for k, v in r.totals.items()} for r in results},
        "report": str(report_path), "questions": str(questions_path)}, indent=2) + "\n") if args.all else None
    print(f"wrote {report_path} and {questions_path}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Rule tests on a synthetic employer. Nothing here comes from the six real employer files."""

import csv
import json
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "skills" / "class-code-assistant" / "scripts"))

from cca import records, render  # noqa: E402
from cca.guide import Guide  # noqa: E402
from cca.rules import WorksheetError, allocate, infer_employer_codes  # noqa: E402

HP = json.loads((ROOT / "skills/class-code-assistant/references/house_practice.json").read_text())

GUIDE = """# Test guide

Edition of March 2030.

**CG-01. Premium basis.** Not used.

**CG-04. C-110 Clerical office employees.** Office work.

**CG-30. Z-100 Field work.** Work at sites.

**CG-31. Z-200 Other field work.** Different work at sites.

**CG-32. T-610 Courier drivers.** Driving routes.
"""


def write_csv(path, header, rows):
    with open(path, "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(header)
        w.writerows(rows)


class Employer:
    """Build a throwaway employer folder."""

    def __init__(self, register, split, travel=False):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.dir = Path(self.tmp.name) / "test-co"
        self.dir.mkdir()
        rows = "\n".join(f"| {c} | {n} | {a} |" for c, (n, a) in split.items())
        (self.dir / "application.md").write_text(
            f"# Test Co: payroll\n\nApplication APP-T-1, signed by Pat Doe.\n\n| Code | Employees | Payroll |\n|---|---|---|\n{rows}\n")
        (self.dir / "business-description.md").write_text("# Test Co\n\nAudit period January 1, 2030 to December 31, 2030.\n")
        header = ["employee_id", "name", "position", "wages_paid"] + (["travel_days", "travel_allowance_paid"] if travel else [])
        write_csv(self.dir / "payroll-register.csv", header, register)

    def csv(self, name, header, rows):
        write_csv(self.dir / name, header, rows)
        return self

    def run(self, ws):
        return allocate(Guide(GUIDE), HP, records.load(self.dir), ws)


def person(code, **kw):
    return {"duty_code": code, "basis": "test duties", "records": [], **kw}


class GuideTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_paragraph_refs_and_edition(self):
        g = Guide(GUIDE)
        self.assertEqual(g.edition, "March 2030")
        self.assertEqual(g.ref_for("Z-100"), "CG-30")
        self.assertEqual(g.ref_for("C-110"), "CG-04")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            g.ref_for("Q-999")


class RuleTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_owner_with_field_work_counted_at_flat_amount(self):
        e = Employer([["E1", "Owner", "Owner", "120000.00"]], {"C-110": (1, "120000.00")})
        r = e.run({"employees": {"E1": person("C-110")},
                   "owners": {"E1": {"included": True, "field_work": True, "field_code": "Z-100", "basis": "on site"}}})
        self.assertEqual(r.totals, {"Z-100": Decimal("63700.00")})
        self.assertFalse(r.accepts_employer_split)

    def test_travel_allowance_cap_and_zero_days(self):
        e = Employer([["E1", "A", "Tech", "1000.00", "10", "600.00"],
                      ["E2", "B", "Tech", "1000.00", "10", "470.00"],
                      ["E3", "C", "Tech", "1000.00", "0", "50.00"]],
                     {"Z-100": (3, "3000.00")}, travel=True)
        r = e.run({"employees": {i: person("Z-100") for i in ("E1", "E2", "E3")}})
        # E1: 600 - 10*47 = 130 payroll; E2: exactly at cap, 0; E3: no travel days, all 50 is payroll.
        self.assertEqual(r.totals["Z-100"], Decimal("3180.00"))
        self.assertEqual(sorted(a.amount for a in r.adjustments), [Decimal("50.00"), Decimal("130.00")])
        self.assertTrue(any("no travel days" in o.why for o in r.open_items))

    def test_uninsured_subcontractor_60_percent_by_certificate_dates(self):
        e = (Employer([["E1", "A", "Crew", "1000.00"]], {"Z-100": (1, "1000.00")})
             .csv("subcontractor-payments.csv", ["date", "subcontractor", "work", "invoice", "amount_paid"],
                  [["2030-02-01", "Acme", "framing", "I1", "1000.00"],
                   ["2030-08-01", "Acme", "framing", "I2", "333.33"],
                   ["2030-03-01", "Nocert", "roofing", "I3", "100.00"],
                   ["2029-12-31", "Nocert", "roofing", "I0", "999.00"]])
             .csv("insurance-certificates.csv", ["subcontractor", "certificate_no", "coverage_from", "coverage_to"],
                  [["Acme Ltd", "C1", "2030-01-01", "2030-06-30"]]))
        r = e.run({"employees": {"E1": person("Z-100")},
                   "subcontract_work_codes": {"framing": "Z-100", "roofing": "Z-200"},
                   "subcontractor_certificate_matches": {"Acme": "Acme Ltd"}})
        self.assertEqual(r.totals["Z-100"], Decimal("1200.00"))  # 1000 + 60% of 333.33 = 200.00 (199.998 rounded)
        self.assertEqual(r.totals["Z-200"], Decimal("60.00"))

    def test_no_split_whole_pay_to_most_hours(self):

"""Check the deliverables against the assignment's format rules. Exit status 1 on any failure.

Checks: the six codes CSVs (exact header, cents, no zero rows, rationale_ref as printed in the guide); CSV totals match
the report's allocation tables; one report and one question section per employer; every adjustment in the report is
named in that employer's questions; no employer names or IDs are hard-coded in the Skill's code; interview exports
are unchanged since they were committed.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from cca.guide import Guide  # noqa: E402

HEADER = ["class_code", "payroll_allocated", "rationale_ref"]
CENTS = re.compile(r"^\d+\.\d{2}$")


def sections(text):
    parts = re.split(r"^## (.+)$", text, flags=re.M)
    return {parts[i].strip(): parts[i + 1] for i in range(1, len(parts), 2)}


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="deliverables", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--guide", default=".cache/sources/classification-guide.md", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--employers", default=".cache/sources/employers", type=Path)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    failures, checks = [], 0

    def check(ok, message):
        nonlocal checks
        checks += 1
        if not ok:
            failures.append(message)

    guide = Guide(args.guide.read_text())
    slugs = sorted(p.name for p in args.employers.iterdir() if p.is_dir())
    report = (args.out / "audit-report.md").read_text()
    questions = (args.out / "audit-questions.md").read_text()
    rep_sections, q_sections = sections(report), sections(questions)
    names = {}

    for slug in slugs:
        app = (args.employers / slug / "application.md").read_text()
        name = re.search(r"^#\s*([^:\n]+)", app, re.M).group(1).strip()
        names[slug] = name
        path = args.out / "codes" / f"{slug}.csv"
        check(path.exists(), f"{path} is missing")
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        with open(path, newline="") as f:
            rows = list(csv.reader(f))
        check(rows and rows[0] == HEADER, f"{path}: header must be exactly {','.join(HEADER)}")
        body = rows[1:]
        check(len({r[0] for r in body}) == len(body), f"{path}: a class code appears more than once")
        totals = {}
        for r in body:
            check(len(r) == 3, f"{path}: row {r} does not have 3 columns")
            code, amount, ref = r
            check(CENTS.match(amount) is not None, f"{path}: {amount!r} is not dollars to the cent without separators")
            check(Decimal(amount) > 0, f"{path}: {code} has zero payroll")
            check(guide.code_ref.get(code) == ref, f"{path}: {code} rationale_ref {ref!r} is not the guide paragraph "
                                                   f"{guide.code_ref.get(code)!r}")
            totals[code] = Decimal(amount)

        sec = rep_sections.get(name)
        check(sec is not None, f"audit-report.md has no section '## {name}'")
        check(name in q_sections, f"audit-questions.md has no section '## {name}'")
        if sec is None:
            continue
        table = {m[0]: Decimal(m[2].replace(",", "")) for m in
                 re.findall(r"^\| ([A-Z]-\d{3}) \| (CG-\d+) \| [\d,.]+ \| ([\d,.]+) \|", sec, re.M)}
        table = {c: v for c, v in table.items() if v}
        check(table == totals, f"{name}: CSV totals {totals} differ from the report's allocation table {table}")
        adj = re.search(r"### Adjustments\n\n(.*?)\n\n", sec, re.S)
        qtext = q_sections.get(name, "")
        for row in (adj.group(1).splitlines()[2:] if adj else []):
            about = row.split(" | ")[1].split(", invoice")[0]
            check(about in qtext, f"{name}: adjustment about {about!r} has no question naming it")
        check("Employer's split: accepted" in sec or "Employer's split: not accepted" in sec,
              f"{name}: the report does not state whether the employer's split is accepted")

    check(re.search(r"\brate[sd]? (of|at) \d|premium (of|is) \$?\d", report, re.I) is None,
          "audit-report.md appears to state a rate or premium figure")

    skill_code = "\n".join(p.read_text() for p in Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.rglob("*") if p.suffix in {".py", ".json", ".md"})
    for slug, name in names.items():
        check(slug not in skill_code and name not in skill_code, f"the Skill's code or references mention {name}")
    for slug in slugs:
        with open(args.employers / slug / "payroll-register.csv", newline="") as f:
            for r in csv.DictReader(f):
                check(r["employee_id"] not in skill_code and r["name"] not in skill_code,
                      f"the Skill's code or references mention {r['employee_id']} {r['name']}")

    changed = subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "--name-only", "HEAD", "--", "interviews"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    check(changed.returncode == 0 and not changed.stdout.strip(), f"interview exports changed since commit: {changed.stdout}")

    for f in failures:
        print(f"FAIL {f}")
    print(f"{checks - len(failures)}/{checks} checks passed")
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

---
name: class-code-assistant
description: First-pass premium audit for Linden Shore Mutual workers' compensation new business. It reads an employer's payroll register, application, business description, field notes and time records, then assigns company class codes. It allocates payroll to each code, citing the classification guide paragraph and the supporting records, and drafts employer-specific audit questions. Use it when a premium auditor asks to check, classify or allocate an employer's payroll, or to run the first pass on an employer file. It never sets rates or quotes premium.
---

# Class code assistant

This Skill does the first pass that Nadia Brennan, Senior Premium Auditor, reviews before underwriting quotes an
employer. It classifies people and allocates payroll. It does **not** set rates, compute premium or quote.

## Ground rules

- **Use only the company's own rules.** The authoritative rules are the Linden Shore Mutual classification guide
  excerpt (paragraphs `CG-nn`), read from the location in `references/sources.json` on every run. Public
  classification manuals, such as NCCI or state manuals, do not apply and give wrong answers. Never use them.
- **Apply house practice as the auditor stated it.** `references/house-practice.md` records it (HP-1 to HP-12), with
  the Skill's flagged readings (A1 to A6). The numbers are in `references/house_practice.json`.
- **Classify by actual duties, not titles (HP-1).** The records in the file decide, not the employer's application
  (HP-7).
- **Gray areas: propose, explain and flag, never invent.** When neither the guide nor house practice covers a case,
  propose a treatment, write down why, and add an open item for the auditor (HP-10). Never present a proposal as company
  rule.
- **Keep facts apart from assumptions.** Every fact cites the employer record it comes from. Every assumption is an
  open item.

## Inputs

Per employer, one folder named by its slug (for example `acme-roofing`) holding:

| File | Required | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `payroll-register.csv` (`employee_id,name,position,wages_paid`, optional `travel_days,travel_allowance_paid`) | yes | wages per person; out-of-town allowance |
| `application.md` (table of code, employees, payroll; employer's note) | yes | the employer's own split, for comparison |
| a `.md` stating `Audit period <Month D, YYYY> to <Month D, YYYY>` (usually `business-description.md`) | yes | audit period filter |
| `field-notes.md`, `business-description.md` | no | duties, owner status, subcontractors |
| `*timesheet*.csv` (`date,employee_id,work_type,hours`) | no | crew work by type (HP-2, A2) |
| `*sign*in*.csv` (`date,employee_id,site`) | no | clerical job-site days (HP-4, A3) |
| `route-log.csv` (`date,driver_id,ride_along_id`) + `weekly-payroll.csv` (`week_start,week_end,employee_id,gross_pay`) | no | whole-week route split (HP-2, A1) |
| `subcontractor-payments.csv` (`date,subcontractor,work,invoice,amount_paid`) + `insurance-certificates.csv` (`subcontractor,certificate_no,coverage_from,coverage_to`) | no | uninsured subcontractors (HP-5, A5) |

Other files are listed in the report as not used. Give the reason in the worksheet's `unused_records`.

Plus one **worksheet** per employer, `deliverables/worksheets/<slug>.json`, holding the analyst's judgments (step 3).

## How to run

From the repository root, with Python 3.10 or later and no other dependencies:

1. **Fetch and scaffold.** Run `python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --init-worksheet <slug>`. This
   downloads the guide and employer files into `.cache/sources/` and writes an empty worksheet listing every person,
   work type, site and subcontracted trade that needs a decision.
2. **Read everything.** Read the guide (`.cache/sources/classification-guide.md`) and every file in
   `.cache/sources/employers/<slug>/`. Note which statements are documented, and where the employer's application
   disagrees with its own records.
3. **Fill in the worksheet** following `references/worksheet.md`. For each person, record the code that describes
   what they actually do, a `basis` citing the record, and the `records` relied on. Map each timesheet work type, job
   site and subcontracted trade to a guide code. Use `null` for a site whose work no code describes. Record owners,
   documented facts, confirmations to ask the employer for, and open items for gray areas. Do **not** do arithmetic
   here; the engine applies the house rules.
4. **Run.** Use `python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --employer <slug>` for one employer, or `--all`
   for every employer folder at the source. Add `--local <dir>` to use a local copy laid out as
   `<dir>/classification-guide.md` and `<dir>/employers/<slug>/`, instead of fetching.
5. **Check.** Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` and
   `python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/validate.py`. Then read the report section and the questions as the
   auditor would, and fix the worksheet, not the outputs, if anything is wrong.
6. **Hand over** to the auditor for review (HP-11). The output is a first pass, not audit work.

## Outputs

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `deliverables/codes/<slug>.csv` | Exactly `class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref`. One row per code carrying payroll, dollars to the cent, `rationale_ref` = the guide paragraph describing the code |
| `deliverables/audit-report.md` (`--all`) or `deliverables/runs/<slug>-audit-report.md` | Call-first order with reasons. Per employer: whether the employer's split is accepted and the records that decision rests on, the allocation against the employer's split, where and why they differ, every adjustment with person or payment, amount and records, an employee-by-employee basis, documented facts, open items, and notes on unused records |
| `deliverables/audit-questions.md` (or `deliverables/runs/<slug>-audit-questions.md`) | Per employer, questions naming the person, subcontractor or record, and the document needed. Every adjustment and every record relied on is covered (HP-9) |
| `deliverables/run-manifest.json` (`--all`) | Fetch time, guide sha256 and totals per employer, for traceability |

## Error behaviour

The run stops with `error: ...` and a non-zero exit, writing nothing for that employer, when:

- the guide, the payroll register, the application split or the audit period statement is missing or unreadable;
- a CSV lacks a required column;
- the worksheet is missing, does not list exactly the register's employees, leaves a decision unfilled, or names a
  class code the guide does not describe;
- a timesheet work type, an over-threshold sign-in site or a subcontracted trade has no worksheet mapping. The engine
  will not guess one.

Conditions the records can't settle become open items and do not stop the run: a tie in hours or site days, a
certificate name mismatch, an allowance with no travel days, weekly pay that does not sum to the register, a sign-in on
a fixed holiday, or a threshold met where no code describes the site work.

## Supporting files

- `references/house-practice.md`: the audit team's unwritten rules from the interview, with timestamps, plus this
  Skill's readings A1 to A6.
- `references/house_practice.json`: the numeric parameters (flat owner amount, day threshold, subcontractor share,
  allowance cap).
- `references/sources.json`: where the guide and employer files are kept.
- `references/worksheet.md`: the worksheet fields and how to fill them.
- `scripts/fetch_sources.py`: downloads the sources; standard library only, no credentials.
- `scripts/run.py`: the command-line entry point. `scripts/cca/` holds the guide parser, record loader, rule engine
  and renderer.
- `scripts/validate.py`: checks the deliverables against the required formats.

# Employer worksheet (`deliverables/worksheets/<slug>.json`)

The worksheet holds the judgments that need a reader: what each person actually does, and which guide code describes a
type of work. The engine does everything else from the records: the thresholds, splits, flat amounts, caps,
subcontractor shares and comparison with the employer. Start from `run.py --init-worksheet <slug>`.

Every code must be one the guide describes. Every judgment cites the record it rests on. If a record does not settle a
judgment, make the best-supported proposal and add an `open_items` entry; do not leave it implied.

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `employees.<id>.duty_code` | The code describing the person's **actual** duties from the file (HP-1). For crew with timesheets, give the expected code; the timesheets then decide. For office staff, give `C-110`; the sign-in log then applies the five-day test. |
| `employees.<id>.basis` | One or two sentences: what the person does, the record and date that show it, and the guide paragraph. Say so when the only evidence is a job title. |
| `employees.<id>.records` | Files the basis rests on. The payroll register is added automatically. |
| `employees.<id>.field_code` | Optional. Overrides the site-based code for a clerical person who meets the job-site threshold. |
| `owners.<id or name>` | `included` (no election of exclusion), `field_work`, `field_code`, `basis`, `records`. Excluded owners are listed for the record only. |
| `work_type_codes` | Timesheet `work_type` to code. |
| `site_codes` | Sign-in `site` to code; `null` when no code in the guide describes the work there. |
| `route_code` | Code for route ride-along weeks, when a route log exists. |
| `subcontract_work_codes` | Subcontracted `work` to code. |
| `subcontractor_certificate_matches` | Payee name to certificate name, when they differ. Always raised as an open item. |
| `facts` | `{fact, record}` statements the report lists as documented. |
| `confirmations` | `{about, question}` employer questions for records relied on that the engine does not know about, such as an owner's exclusion election. Name the person or record and the document needed. |
| `open_items` | `{about, proposal, why, records, employer_question?, merge_with?}`. `merge_with` adds context to an item the engine raises for the same person. |
| `unused_records` | File name to the reason it was not used. |

# Class Code and Premium Audit Assistant

A reusable Agent Skill that does the first pass of a Linden Shore Mutual premium audit on any employer file. It
suggests the company's class codes, allocates payroll to them with the guide paragraph and supporting records for each
decision, and drafts the questions the auditor should put to the employer. It classifies and allocates payroll only; it
does not set rates or quote premium.

## Interview rule

**Interview rule.** You conduct the stakeholder interview yourself, and the questions are yours. Do not connect a coding
agent or any other AI to the interview to run, script, or automate it. The interview transcript is assessed together
with the code; a project whose interview was run by an agent is not scored.

- This is a real-case Challenge, closer to client work. The course rule is to plan for at most 3 conversations with the stakeholder, so prepare before each conversation and ask completely.
- The employer files and the company's classification rules are not in this repository. Ask Nadia Brennan, the
  premium auditor you interview, where they are, and read them from there during each run.
- No implementation or runtime is supplied; choose and document the dependencies your Skill needs.
- Export your interview as the original Markdown, save one final complete file per session under `interviews/`, and
  commit it with your code. Do not rewrite the export.

## Layout

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `interviews/` | Original interview exports, unchanged |
| `skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md` | The Skill: inputs, steps, outputs, error behaviour |
| `skills/class-code-assistant/references/` | House practice from the interview, its parameters, source locations, worksheet guide |
| `skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/` | Fetcher, engine (`cca/`), runner and validator |
| `deliverables/worksheets/<slug>.json` | The analyst's per-employer judgments (duty codes, work and site mappings, facts, open items) |
| `deliverables/codes/<slug>.csv`, `audit-report.md`, `audit-questions.md` | The required outputs |
| `tests/` | Rule tests on a synthetic employer |

## Setup

Python 3.10 or later; standard library only, so there is nothing to install. The runner downloads the classification
guide and the employer files from the Google Drive locations Nadia Brennan gave in interview 1
(`skills/class-code-assistant/references/sources.json`) into `.cache/sources/` on every run. The cache is git-ignored.
The links are view-only shares, so no credentials are used or stored.

## Run

```sh
# all six employers: fetches sources, writes deliverables/codes/*.csv, audit-report.md, audit-questions.md
python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --all

# one employer: writes deliverables/codes/<slug>.csv and deliverables/runs/<slug>-audit-{report,questions}.md
python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --employer severn-homebuilders
```

Add `--local <dir>` to run from a local copy laid out as `<dir>/classification-guide.md` and
`<dir>/employers/<slug>/`, instead of fetching.

### A new employer

1. Put the employer's folder (payroll register, application, business description, field notes, any timesheets, sign-in
   or route logs, and any subcontractor payments or certificates) at the source location, or in a local copy.
2. `python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --init-worksheet <slug>` writes
   `deliverables/worksheets/<slug>.json`, listing every decision the records need.
3. Fill it in from the records, following `skills/class-code-assistant/references/worksheet.md`.
4. `python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run.py --employer <slug>`, then run the checks below.

## Verification

Commands run on the committed revision, with their results:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` | 13 tests OK. They cover the guide parser, owner flat amount, allowance cap and zero-day allowance, the 60% uninsured subcontractor share with certificate dates and name mismatch, the five-day clerical threshold, the threshold with no applicable code, an unmapped site raising an error, the no-split rule, the whole-week route split, unknown-code rejection, question coverage, the CSV format and split inference. All use a synthetic employer. |
| `python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/validate.py` | 165/165 checks pass. It checks CSV header, cents and zero rows, `rationale_ref` against the guide, CSV totals against the report, a section per employer in both files, every adjustment named in that employer's questions, a stated accept/not-accept decision, no rate or premium figures, no employer names or IDs in the Skill code, and an unchanged interview export. |
| `run.py --all` (fresh fetch) and `--employer larkspur-lane-bistro --local .cache/sources` | Same CSV for that employer either way. |
| Error paths | A missing worksheet, an unfilled scaffold and a missing guide each stop with a clear `error:` and exit 1. |
| Hand check | Patuxent Electric E-510 (306,024.85 + 63,700.00 + 3 × 720.00 + 390.00 = 372,274.85), Severn Homebuilders subcontractor additions (60% of 41,155.65 = 24,693.39 H-420; 60% of 31,645.65 = 18,987.39 R-310) and the Bay Crest Exteriors totals were recomputed by hand from the source files and match. |

Not verified. Each of these is an open item in the report:

- The readings of house practice (A1 to A6 in `references/house-practice.md`) have not been confirmed by the auditor.
- The code given to a clerical person who passes the five-day test (Teresa Lindqvist, Dana Whitcomb) is the Skill's
  proposal.
- The call-first ranking rule is the Skill's own; the auditor has not said how she prioritises calls.
- The employer-level comparison relies on an inferred per-person reading of each application. That reading is unique for
  all six employers, but it is still an inference.
- The Drive fetcher depends on Google's public folder-view page; if its markup changes, fetching fails loudly and
  `--local` still works.

## First-pass decisions on the employers' own splits

| Employer | Employer's split | Rests on |
|---|---|---|
| Harbor Point Legal | Accepted | payroll register; field notes (all office work). Tomas Reyes's six condominium sign-ins are an open item. |
| Larkspur Lane Bistro | Accepted | payroll register; field notes (catering crew does off-site events, CG-42). The crew's restaurant shifts have no time record: open item. |
| Bay Crest Exteriors | Not accepted | crew timesheets (eight crew members on roofing, siding and gutters, not office work); site sign-in log (estimator, 9 site days) |
| Patuxent Electric | Not accepted | business description (owner not excluded); field notes and site sign-in log (owner does field work); register travel columns (allowance above 47.00 per day) |
| Severn Homebuilders | Not accepted | site sign-in log (office manager, 11 site days); subcontractor payments against insurance certificates (Tidewater Drywall has none; Kent Island's lapsed 2026-01-31) |
| Annapolis Courier | Not accepted | route log and weekly payroll (both dispatchers rode along; whole weeks moved to T-610) |

I built the reusable Skill and ran it on all six employers. Every source file and the classification guide were reachable from the links Nadia gave in the interview, so nothing had to be left as groundwork. The interview export is committed unchanged, and nothing was pushed. All 13 unit tests pass and the format validator passes 165 of 165 checks.

## What the Skill does
- **Reads the sources fresh on every run** from Nadia's Drive links, using only Python's standard library.
- **Uses only the company guide's own paragraph numbers** (CG-04 and so on) in `rationale_ref`. Nadia said she didn't know of identifiers, but the guide prints them and the assignment requires them.
- **Applies house practice only as Nadia stated it.** I wrote her rules down with interview timestamps in [house-practice.md](skills/class-code-assistant/references/house-practice.md). Six places where I had to interpret her words are labelled as my readings, and each one becomes an open item wherever it changes an allocation.
- **Keeps judgment separate from arithmetic.** The judgments sit in one worksheet per employer, each citing the record it rests on. The engine then applies the thresholds, splits, flat amounts, caps and subcontractor share the same way for every employer. No employer data is in the code, and the validator checks that.
- **Produces the required outputs:** the six [codes CSVs](deliverables/codes/), [audit-report.md](deliverables/audit-report.md) and [audit-questions.md](deliverables/audit-questions.md). The report shows the allocation against the employer's split, each adjustment to the cent with its records, an employee-by-employee basis, facts kept apart from open items, and which employers to call first.

## Do I accept each employer's split?
| Employer | Split | What the decision rests on |
|---|---|---|
| Harbor Point Legal | **Accept** | Register and field notes show all office work. Tomas Reyes's 6 condominium sign-ins are an open item. |
| Larkspur Lane Bistro | **Accept** | Field notes put the catering crew under the caterer code. Their restaurant shifts have no time record (open item). Gross receipts were not used. |
| Bay Crest Exteriors | **Reject** | Crew timesheets show 8 field workers, not 3. Owen Petrakis, titled "Roofer", logged mostly siding hours, so he moves to the siding code. The estimator has 9 site days and moves out of clerical. 319,158.10 leaves C-110. |
| Patuxent Electric | **Reject** | The owner isn't excluded and does field work (214 site days), so he is counted at the flat 63,700.00 under E-510 instead of 118,000.00 under clerical. Travel allowance above 47.00 a day adds 2,550.00 of payroll. |
| Severn Homebuilders | **Reject** | The office manager has 11 site days, so she moves to H-420. Tidewater Drywall has no certificate, and Kent Island's certificate lapsed on 2026-01-31; 60% of those payments adds 43,680.78. |
| Annapolis Courier | **Reject** | The route log shows both dispatchers rode along, so 30,078.05 of their pay moves to the courier code by whole weeks. |

**Call first:** Bay Crest Exteriors, then Patuxent Electric. The ranking is by how much payroll the records move away from the employer's split; that rule is mine. Severn Homebuilders is close behind (163k against Patuxent's 184k) and depends most on documents the employer has to send.

## Not yet confirmed
- The six readings of house practice (A1 to A6) are my interpretation and need Nadia's confirmation.
- The code I gave Teresa Lindqvist (Bay Crest estimator) and Dana Whitcomb (Severn office manager) after they passed the five-day site test is a proposal.
- The employer's per-person split is inferred from the application totals. It came out unique for all six employers, but it is still an inference.

## Missing information for the next interview
1. **Code after the clerical test.** Which code replaces C-110 once a clerical person reaches five or more job-site days. Also whether client sites, closings or errand stops count as "job sites", and whether the five days count across the whole audit period.
2. **Meaning of "by whole weeks"** for dispatcher ride-alongs. I assumed one ride-along day sends that whole week's pay to the courier code.
3. **Mixed crew work.** How to pick the single code when timesheets show more than one kind of work. I used the code with the most hours. Also whether the guide's CG-07 division of payroll is ever allowed.
4. **Owner flat amount details.** Which code it goes under, and whether it applies whatever the owner's actual pay (it lowers Patuxent's payroll) and for a partial year.
5. **Subcontractor coverage.** Whether a certificate is matched to the payment date or the work date, and how to treat a name mismatch on a certificate (Kent Island Roofing against "Kent Island Roofing & Siding LLC").
6. **Allowance with no travel days.** How to treat an allowance paid with zero recorded travel days (Kyle Brandt, 390.00), and how her 47.00 cap relates to the guide's exclusion for documented reimbursements.
7. **Supervisors and temporary workers.** She has no rule yet, and working foremen exist: Darnell Price at Bay Crest and Garrett Holm at Severn.
8. **Restaurant shifts by caterers.** Whether a catering crew's restaurant shifts change their code, and whether receipts ever matter.
9. **Doubtful records.** How to treat entries that look wrong, such as Teresa Lindqvist's sign-in on 2025-12-25. That one day decides her code.
10. **Rule sources.** Confirmation that the CG-nn numbers are the references to cite, and that the July 2025 edition covers the whole audit period. She also said the audit period is in the payroll register; it is actually in the business description.
11. **Call-first criteria.** What she weighs when choosing which two employers to call before Friday.
